sources.entry: The Lounge - Self-hosted web IRC client. (Demo, Source Code) MIT Nodejs/Docker

summary.one_liner: The Lounge is a self-hosted, always-connected web IRC client that runs on Node.js and is available as a Docker image.
summary.what_it_does: The Lounge is a web-based IRC client meant to be hosted on your own server. It stays connected to IRC networks while you are offline, so messages are kept and you can resume where you left off from any device. The README describes a responsive interface that works on desktops, smartphones and tablets. It lists push notifications, link previews and new-message markers as features. It runs anywhere Node.js runs. The Lounge is the community-managed fork of Shout by Mattias Erming.
use_cases: Stay connected to IRC channels while offline
Use IRC from a phone or tablet in a browser
Self-host a web chat client for a community
Receive push notifications for IRC mentions
Resume IRC conversations across multiple devices
how_to_run: Install the latest Node.js LTS version (Yarn recommended)
git clone the repository and cd thelounge
Alternatively, see the website for stable release and Docker installation methods
notable: Always-connected server keeps IRC sessions alive while the browser is closed
Fork of Shout, maintained by a community team
Responsive web interface for desktop and mobile
caveats: The README warns the source-from-git version is not production-ready and should be run at your own risk
Not recommended to run as root
keywords: share a chat with my team
